analysis.body:
# Retail AI Adoption and Deployment

According to the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, 15.2% of retail trade firms reported using AI in the last two weeks as of the latest measurement period, a slight decline from 15.5% in the prior period. This baseline adoption figure, collected alongside all other sectors, provides a measured picture of how widely AI tools have penetrated the industry.

Retailers are deploying AI across several functional areas, though the actual work being done varies considerably by vendor and use case. IHL Group reports that 85% of retailers modernizing point-of-sale systems met or exceeded return-on-investment expectations, with cloud-native and API-driven tools lifting conversion and transaction values. A model for a $1 billion retailer projected $44 million in annual financial impact from such modernization, though integration challenges persist. Batteries Plus offers a concrete example, rolling out three AI tools across its 800-plus-location network by September 2026: Savannah for franchise prospecting, Edison for bilingual customer call handling, and Wattson for product search linked to point-of-sale systems.

IHL Group's research identifies a structural problem: most retail AI budgets fund the wrong infrastructure layer first, and vendors' claims about having AI do not predict actual platform quality. The firm emphasizes that retailers should test explainability on real items, control over automation by category and channel, and safeguards separating market-responsive from individualized pricing, areas where governance, adoption, and compliance risks diverge. The same analyst found that inventory distortion totaled $1.7 trillion while empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion, suggesting AI agents are now being deployed to address these costly problems.

The NRF, as the trade body tracking store technology, frames the adoption challenge as cultural and organizational: retailers must build the culture, influence, and trust needed to move AI initiatives beyond experimentation. Coresight Research, the retail and technology research firm with deep China expertise, convenes an exclusive forum on AI opportunities and challenges for consumer-focused businesses and has published work on how data and AI transform retail strategies and organizational structures.

Retailers considering deployment should recognize that raw adoption statistics mask implementation complexity and misaligned vendor incentives. The data shows measurable ROI is achievable in specific areas—particularly point-of-sale modernization and inventory management—but success depends on vendor selection discipline, clear governance frameworks, and organizational readiness to move beyond pilots to enterprise-scale operations.
